thesis: Claims of maximal power and goodness face an explanatory burden; neither faith nor disbelief cancels practical duties.
role: Testing responsibility at the limit of power

ideas.statement: Creation and irresistible power do not by themselves establish unrestricted moral authority.
Logical defense, evidential plausibility and an actual explanation differ; proposed theodicies require scrutiny.
Suffering does not establish deserved guilt, and later compensation need not undo loss.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: Job challenges convenient explanations of suffering and supports the possibility of religious protest.
Different conceptions of deity change the question, and defining every attributed act as good risks emptying goodness of meaning.
Human duties can survive theological uncertainty, and different metaphysical grounds can support practical cooperation.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: The chapter neither proves nor disproves God; believers and nonbelievers can cooperate through different ultimate grounds.

audit.notes: All assigned units read. Claims remain bounded; hypothetical cases are not empirical evidence.
